ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Prior immune HIT

An adult had confirmed immune-mediated heparin-induced thrombocytopenia three weeks ago and now requires anticoagulation for a new thrombus. A resident proposes enoxaparin because its heparin chains are shorter. Which consideration most strongly argues against that substitution?

  1. Antibodies may cross-react with LMWH-associated complexes
  2. LMWH has no anticoagulant effect in venous thrombosis
  3. LMWH invariably depletes vitamin K stores
  4. Short heparin chains cannot bind antithrombin
  5. LMWH directly activates platelet P2Y12 receptors
Answer and explanation

Antibodies may cross-react with LMWH-associated complexes

Recent immune HIT is a contraindication; LMWH is not a safe automatic substitute.

Option explanations

Antibodies may cross-react with LMWH-associated complexes: Recent immune HIT is a contraindication; LMWH is not a safe automatic substitute.

LMWH has no anticoagulant effect in venous thrombosis: Enoxaparin is effective for venous thromboembolism when appropriate.

LMWH invariably depletes vitamin K stores: Vitamin K depletion is not its mechanism.

Short heparin chains cannot bind antithrombin: The pentasaccharide sequence permits antithrombin binding.

LMWH directly activates platelet P2Y12 receptors: P2Y12 activation is not the relevant immune mechanism.
